newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-LAT FIRMS SLIGHTLY AFTER BOUT OF WEAKNESS.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-LAT FIRMS SLIGHTLY AFTER BOUT OF WEAKNESS.

text.p: The lat was trading back up to 0.5914/19 dollars on Friday after sliding to near 0.60 after a large foreign investor flooded the market with lats by buying dollars after the maturity of government bonds.
Dealers said that after the maturity of a $40 million two-year bond that was launched in 1995, the investor converted the lats into dollars.
They said that around $20 million to $30 million of lats was sold, pushing the price down to its low levels.
The average usual daily turnover of the market is around five million dollars, dealers said. The lat sales took place gradually over the last week and a half, dealers said.
"This was very big for the Latvian market," said one trader.
Dealers said they now expected the lat to stabilse around 0.5917 but were not sure whether it would firm again to its more recent levels of around 0.57.
"There are reasons to buy and there are reasons to sell," said one trader.
He said there may be renewed demand for the lat as Russian gas giant Gazprom has to still to pay for the stake it bought in Latvian Gas.
The stake must be paid for by a meeting of Latvian Gas shareholders, due on August 15.
